details: Bitcoin has experienced a significant downturn, falling below the $70,000 and $68,000 price levels, and dropping below its 200-week moving average for the first time since August 19. This sharp decline triggered over $1.3 billion in crypto futures liquidations across the market within 24 hours, with Bitcoin alone accounting for $677 million. The broader crypto market capitalization also declined by over 2.43%.
title: Bitcoin Crashes Below Key Support Levels Amid Mass Liquidations

details: The crypto market's recent plunge is largely attributed to prevailing "macro risk-off conditions." A stronger US dollar (DXY topping 103), rising US 10-year Treasury yields (hitting 5.125%), and higher-than-expected US inflation data (October PPI rose 6.5% year over year) have increased bets on a potential half-point Federal Reserve interest rate hike in December, prompting investors to pull away from risk assets like cryptocurrencies.
title: Macroeconomic Pressures Fueling Crypto Market Sell-Off

details: Ethereum (ETH) has fallen below the $2,000 mark for the first time since August, with reports indicating that the Ethereum Foundation sold 5,000 ETH over a five-day period, contributing to the downward pressure on Ether's price amidst the broader market sell-off.
title: Ethereum Foundation Sells ETH as Price Dips Below $2,000

details: The cryptocurrency market is facing further headwinds from significant outflows in exchange-traded funds (ETFs). Spot XRP ETFs have seen outflows exceeding $18 million in just two days, while US spot Bitcoin ETFs are cumulatively down $1.56 billion for 2026, contributing to the overall market's downward trajectory.
title: Crypto ETF Outflows Intensify Amid Market Weakness
